column1: 404 | PART IV Business Cycle Theory: The Economy in the Short Run Fiscal Policy Figure 13-16 examines the impact of a fiscal expansion. An increase in government purchases or a cut in taxes shifts the IS curve to the right. As panel (a) illustrates, this shift in the IS curve leads to an increase in the level of income and an increase in the interest rate. These two effects are similar to those in a closed economy. Yet in the large open economy the higher interest rate reduces the net capital outflow, as in panel (b). The fall in the net capital outflow reduces the supply of dollars in the market for foreign exchange. The exchange rate appreciates, as in panel (c). Because domestic goods become more expensive relative to foreign goods, net exports fall.
